title: Renewal & expansion check-in - Lakeview Payments
next_steps: Alex to send updated pricing for dedicated GPU pool and regional add-on (EOD 2027-08-02)
Samir to run 1-hour benchmark on customer's test dataset in eu-west-1 and share results (by 2027-08-04)
Priya to share SOC 2 + data residency docs and contract amendment template (by 2027-08-03)
Schedule technical deep-dive for Marcus and infra team (tentatively 2027-08-06)
Nina to confirm procurement timeline and PO process (by 2027-08-05)
action_items: Alex Morgan: prepare dedicated capacity pricing + region SKUs (due 2027-08-02)
Samir Patel: run perf benchmark in eu-west-1 with 512 token avg seq (due 2027-08-04)
Priya Kaur: share security pack (SOC2, ISO, KMS integration notes) and contract amendment (due 2027-08-03)
Marcus Liu: provide sample traffic profile and current p99 latency SLOs (due 2027-08-01)
Nina Park: confirm contract signing timeline / PO workflow (due 2027-08-05)
summary: Quarterly renewal/expansion check-in focused on upgrading to dedicated capacity, adding eu-west-1 region, and aligning contract extension timelines. Lakeview is seeing increased traffic and wants predictable latency and data residency in Europe. Redwood to provide pricing, run benchmarks, and share compliance docs. Next steps agreed.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hi everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Jared Kim: Jared here, hey.
[00:08] Elena Rodriguez: Elena present.
[00:09] Marcus Liu: Marcus - SRE.
[00:10] Nina Park: Nina from procurement.
[00:12] Samir Patel: Samir from Redwood (SE).
[00:15] Priya Kaur: Priya CSM, on mute mostly.

[00:25] Alex Morgan: Cool. Agenda - renewal and expansion, lakeview growth, dedicated capacity options and eu-west-1 region. We have about 45 minutes.

[00:35] Jared Kim: Yeah, high level - traffic up ~2.3x q/q, our token volume is moving up, and a chunk of new clients are EU-based so we need european region and data residency. Also procurement wants to lock renewal + extension with committed capacity.

[00:55] Alex Morgan: Makes sense. Do you have current numbers or a projection?

[01:00] Marcus Liu: We can share. Right now 200 rps peak and avg seq lengths about 380 tokens, with spikes to 700 on some flows. p95 is fine but p99 sometimes drifts to 1.1s which is marginal for checkout flows.

[01:22] Samir Patel: Okay, that's helpful. For p99 target under 500-600ms we'd recommend moving to a dedicated GPU pool and enabling prefix cache + batching tuned to your seq distribution. Quantization also helps but we should test on your model.

[01:38] Elena Rodriguez: Are there latency tradeoffs vs cost we should expect?

[01:42] Samir Patel: Yeah, generally dedicated gives more predictable latency - lower variance. Cost per token increases a bit compared to oversubscribed hosted, but overall unit cost can drop if you tune batching and use KV cache effectively. We'll model it in the price sheet.

[02:00] Alex Morgan: We're hearing a procurement ask to commit to a 12-month extension with a reserved pool that covers expected peak plus 20% buffer. Nina, is that the ask?

[02:09] Nina Park: Correct. Need committed min and ability to burst and also to confirm data residency for EU. Also want the amendment to include exit terms and audit logs.

[02:20] Priya Kaur: For data residency we can provision private tenancy in eu-west-1, and we have KMS integrations; I'll attach the SOC2 and our KMS docs.

[02:32] Jared Kim: Great. Samir, you mentioned benchmarking - can you run a runbook against our test payload in eu-west-1? We want to see p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.

[02:43] Samir Patel: Absolutely. I'll spin up a reserved pool mirror in eu-west-1 and run the test. I'll need a sample of your payload and the inference config (max tokens, sampling settings). Marcus, can you share that?

[02:53] Marcus Liu: Yeah I'll drop a sanitized payload and current configs in the shared drive.

[03:00] Alex Morgan: On the pricing side - we'll provide two options: 1) 12-month reserved capacity with discounted commit, and 2) 6-month with higher rate + add-on for region. We'll include burst policies and SLAs.

[03:12] Elena Rodriguez: What SLA uplift do we get with dedicated?

[03:16] Samir Patel: Typical is 99.9% uptime plus latency SLO options. We can set p99 SLOs with automated routing fallback to hosted models if the dedicated pool has pressure - that keeps your app online but may have slightly higher latency.

[03:32] Jared Kim: That fallback behavior is important - we need guaranteed correctness and also a way to prefer lower-latency path.

[03:37] Samir Patel: We can route by policy - prefer dedicated until CPU/GPU saturation threshold then fallback to a verified compatible model. There's also canary rollouts for model changes.

[03:50] Marcus Liu: One thing - encryption keys. Our security team wants to manage keys in our KMS and ensure logs don't leave region. Is that supported for private deployment?

[03:59] Priya Kaur: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS and can configure log retention and region controls. For hosted accounts we also have KMS but we can do BYOK for Private. I'll send the integration notes.

[04:12] Nina Park: Procurement will need a sample contract amendment. Can you include terms for extra regions as an add-on SKU?

[04:18] Alex Morgan: We'll draft an amendment with region SKUs and burst allowances, and include the PO workflow.

[04:24] Elena Rodriguez: Onboarding - how long to get eu-west-1 pool live?

[04:28] Samir Patel: Once contract and capacity sizing are agreed, typically 2-4 weeks to provision and validate, faster if we can reuse a template and you provide test traffic early. Benchmarks we run in 48-72 hours and then a validation run.

[04:42] Jared Kim: If we sign a 12-month commit with a mid-year increase option, can we add more capacity or region mid-contract?

[04:49] Alex Morgan: Yes, we support amendments and scaling. We'll include pricing bands for mid-term upsizes.

[04:55] Marcus Liu: For the benchmark - can you also simulate cold-start scenarios and cache warming? Our worst-case is after a deploy.

[05:02] Samir Patel: We'll include cold-start and steady-state tests, and measure token throughput per GPU. Also test quantized model variants.

[05:12] Elena Rodriguez: Any risk of vendor lock-in? If we ever wanted to bring something on-prem or another cloud, how portable is the setup?

[05:20] Samir Patel: We provide model/version pinning and export of configs. For Private deployments we can do on-prem or VPC options that give more portability. We can share a migration runbook.

[05:31] Jared Kim: Competitors - FineServe pitched lower MSRP but no EU region yet; MegaCloud AI has EU but higher latency in our tests.

[05:40] Alex Morgan: Understood. We'll make sure the price/perf sheet reflects the tradeoffs.

[05:46] Nina Park: Timeline wise procurement aiming to finalize by Aug 12 to hit vendor review board. That gives you a couple weeks for pricing and docs.

[05:55] Alex Morgan: Ok we'll target to get everything to you by Aug 3 to leave time.

[06:00] Samir Patel: One quick technical note - given your seq length distribution, we may recommend a mix of p3-style instances with larger memory per GPU or enable KV cache with a 256MB prefix store; we'll pick exact kernel/compilation profile after the benchmark.

[06:16] Marcus Liu: Sounds good. Also can you confirm audit log retention windows and whether logs can be pushed to our SIEM?

[06:22] Priya Kaur: Yes, we can push audit logs via secure forwarder to your SIEM and set retention policies per region. I'll include config notes.

[06:30] Alex Morgan: Any other questions?

[06:33] Elena Rodriguez: Nothing from product side.

[06:35] Jared Kim: No.

[06:37] Nina Park: I'll follow up on procurement specifics.

[06:40] Alex Morgan: Recap of next steps: Alex send pricing and amendment draft, Samir run benchmark in eu-west-1, Priya share SOC2/KMS/docs, Marcus provide traffic sample, Nina confirm procurement timeline. We'll aim to reconvene after Samir's benchmark.

[06:56] Alex Morgan: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

[07:00] Meeting ended.
